chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Abu Muhammad al-Razi, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) said to me: 'I dislike for a man that I see his forehead bald, with no mark of prostration in it.'
ai.seo_question: What does the mark of prostration on the forehead signify in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the forehead mark of prostration as a visible testament to consistent devotion, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the physical manifestation of spiritual discipline. This physical sign serves as a humble indicator of one's connection to God, aligning with the broader tradition where bodily acts of worship are seen as reflections of inner sincerity and piety.
